new_statements.rule_in_words: Adioukrou is described (Hérault 1971) as a tone language with High, Mid, Low and a mostly-rising 'modulated' tone; the primary phonology makes no statement about word stress, and the LAPSyD coders therefore code stress as absent ('assumed none'). No first-hand statement locating word stress was found.
new_statements.domain_note: Database coding of the whole language from Hérault 1971; not a first-hand statement. Other opened sources (Hill 1995 fn.4: four tones H, L, falling, rising; Kaul 2006 summary: 2 tones; Hartell 1993: H/L/HL) speak only of tone and are silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to Adioukrou/Adjukru (adj, adio1239) as a whole; LAPSyD's entry is coded from Hérault 1971, whose data are from the Dabou-area variety. Glottolog's ref list for adio1239 also contains Abidji items (Werle 1971, Hager-M'Boua 2014, Vick 1990) which describe abid1235, not Adioukrou; the earlier scan's 'Werle 1971 phonology' is one of these.

tone_statements.citation: Herault, Georges (1981). L’information ségmentale nécessaire à l’élaboration des règles tonales de l’adioukrou. In Précis from the 12th conference on African linguistics. Studies in African Linguistics Suppl. Los Angeles: African Studies Center & Department of Linguistics, University of California (UCLA). pp. 51-54.
tone_statements.quote: Au plan tonal, on démontre facilement l'opposition de deux tons ponctuels, H et B, et de deux tons modules, HB et BH. Une règle de QUANTIFICATION rend compte du downdrift caractéristique de la langue; partout sauf devant pause, les modulés descendants HB sont réduits à H par une règle de PONCTUALISATION. La langue fait usage de tons flottants, notés (H) et (B), tant au niveau lexical que grammatical.
tone_statements.translation: On the tonal level, one easily demonstrates the opposition of two level tones, H and L(B), and two contour tones, HL(HB) and LH(BH). A QUANTIFICATION rule accounts for the downdrift characteristic of the language; everywhere except before pause, falling contours HB are reduced to H by a PUNCTUALISATION rule. The language makes use of floating tones, written (H) and (B), at both the lexical and the grammatical level.
tone_statements.summary: Four tones: level H and L plus contours HL and LH; lexical and grammatical floating tones; both contours downstep a following H; HL surfaces as H except before pause; downdrift.
